info.title: Nexigon Hub API
info.description:
Welcome to the Nexigon Hub API documentation!

Nexigon Hub offers an RPC-style HTTP API.

post.description:
**Group `admin`:** Part of the Admin API, which requires instance administrator permissions. Backward-incompatible changes are more frequent than for other actions.

Query the users of the instance.
Get information about a user.

**Group `admin`:** Part of the Admin API, which requires instance administrator permissions. Backward-incompatible changes are more frequent than for other actions.

Create a new user.

**Group `admin`:** Part of the Admin API, which requires instance administrator permissions. Backward-incompatible changes are more frequent than for other actions.

Delete a user.

**Group `admin`:** Part of the Admin API, which requires instance administrator permissions. Backward-incompatible changes are more frequent than for other actions.

Deactivate a user account.

Admin-only operation. Deactivated users cannot sign in and their API tokens
are rejected. All existing sessions of the user are terminated. Memberships,
tokens, and data are retained and usable again after reactivation. Deactivating
a deactivated user replaces their message, or selects the default message if
`message` is absent. Users cannot deactivate themselves.

**Group `admin`:** Part of the Admin API, which requires instance administrator permissions. Backward-incompatible changes are more frequent than for other actions.

Reactivate a deactivated user account.

Admin-only operation that restores the user's ability to sign in and use
their API tokens.
Set the display name of a user.

**Group `admin`:** Part of the Admin API, which requires instance administrator permissions. Backward-incompatible changes are more frequent than for other actions.

Set whether the user is an instance administrator.

**Group `admin`:** Part of the Admin API, which requires instance administrator permissions. Backward-incompatible changes are more frequent than for other actions.

Set the password of a user.

Admin-only operation that sets the password without requiring the current
one. All existing sessions of the user are invalidated.

**Group `admin`:** Part of the Admin API, which requires instance administrator permissions. Backward-incompatible changes are more frequent than for other actions.

Set the email address of a user.

Admin-only operation that updates the address without verification.

Change the password of the current user.

Requires account credentials in `authorization`, even if the user is
already authenticated.

Reset the password of a user.

This will send an email to the user with a link to reset their password.
Complete the password reset of a user.

Initiate an email-address change for the current user.

Requires account credentials in `authorization`. On success, a verification
link is sent to the new address and a notification is sent to the current address.
Complete an email-address change using a verification token.
Query the tokens of a user.
Query the organizations of a user.
Query the organization invitations of a user.
Query the sessions of a user.
Check the permissions of a user for a given device.
Create a user token.
Delete a user token.

Terminate a user session.

The acting user must own the session; sessions belonging to other
users are not affected.
Register a new user with an email and password.
Complete the registration of a user.
Accept a organization invitation.

**Group `admin`:** Part of the Admin API, which requires instance administrator permissions. Backward-incompatible changes are more frequent than for other actions.

Query the organizations of the instance.
Query the members of an organization.
Query the projects of an organization.
Query the repositories of an organization.
Query the invitations of an organization.

**Group `admin`:** Part of the Admin API, which requires instance administrator permissions. Backward-incompatible changes are more frequent than for other actions.

Create an organization.

**Group `admin`:** Part of the Admin API, which requires instance administrator permissions. Backward-incompatible changes are more frequent than for other actions.

Delete an organization.

**Group `admin`:** Part of the Admin API, which requires instance administrator permissions. Backward-incompatible changes are more frequent than for other actions.

Deactivate an organization.

Admin-only operation. Members and API tokens hold no permissions in a
deactivated organization, except that its administrators can manage its
subscription. Its devices cannot connect, and its repositories are neither
public nor available to devices of other organizations. Members,
tokens, devices, data, and subscriptions are retained, and billing continues.
Reactivation restores access. Deactivating a deactivated organization
replaces its message, or selects the built-in message if `message` is absent.

**Group `admin`:** Part of the Admin API, which requires instance administrator permissions. Backward-incompatible changes are more frequent than for other actions.

Reactivate a deactivated organization.

Admin-only operation that restores access for members, API tokens, and
devices.

**Group `admin`:** Part of the Admin API, which requires instance administrator permissions. Backward-incompatible changes are more frequent than for other actions.

Add a user to an organization.
Remove a user from an organization.
Set whether the user is an administrator of the organization.
Invite a user to an organization.
Delete an invitation to an organization.
Query the audit log of an organization.
List a project's group catalog, including groups without assignments.
Create a group. Case-insensitive name collisions are rejected.
Replace group metadata while retaining its identity and assignments.

Delete a group and its assignments.

Existing operation selectors retain the group identity and continue evaluating
membership. A deleted group is absent from every device.

Atomically add and remove memberships on explicit devices in one project.

Adding an existing membership or removing an absent one is a no-op. A group
cannot appear in both lists. Unrelated memberships are preserved. All devices
and groups must belong to the project; otherwise no memberships change.
Device credentials cannot change groups. Removing a membership does not cancel
work that an operation has already assigned to the device.

**Unstable (feature `device_profiles`).**

List the device profiles of a project.

**Unstable (feature `device_profiles`).**

Get a device profile with the property values of its latest revision.

**Unstable (feature `device_profiles`).**

Create a device profile with its first revision.

**Unstable (feature `device_profiles`).**

Replace the display name and description of a device profile.

Does not create a revision and does not change any device property.

**Unstable (feature `device_profiles`).**

Delete a device profile and remove it from every device.

**Unstable (feature `device_profiles`).**

Save new property values of a device profile as its next revision.

Every device that has the profile in `Latest` mode applies the new values
right away.

**Unstable (feature `device_profiles`).**

List the revisions of a device profile, newest first.

**Unstable (feature `device_profiles`).**

Assign a device profile to the devices of its project that match group
conditions.

Applies once to the devices that match now; devices that match later do not
receive the profile. The profile applies after a device's other profiles, and
devices that already have it keep its position but take the given mode.
Devices that already have the maximum number of profiles are skipped. Requires
permission to change the profiles of every matching device.

**Unstable (feature `device_profiles`).**

Remove a device profile from the devices of its project that match group
conditions.

Requires permission to change the profiles of every matching device that has
the profile.

**Unstable (feature `device_profiles`).**

Start a rollout of a profile revision to the profile's devices in rollout
mode, replacing the profile's current rollout.

Releases the first stage right away. The new rollout runs even if the rollout
it replaces was halted.

**Unstable (feature `device_profiles`).**

Get the rollout of a profile.

**Unstable (feature `device_profiles`).**

List the devices of a profile's rollout, by stage.

**Unstable (feature `device_profiles`).**

Halt the rollout of a profile.

The rollout applies its revision to no further devices and releases no
stages until it is resumed. Halting a halted rollout has no effect.

**Unstable (feature `device_profiles`).**

Resume the halted rollout of a profile where it stopped.

Resuming a running rollout has no effect.

**Unstable (feature `device_profiles`).**

Release the next stage of a running rollout, skipping its guard and the wait
for the previous stage's spread.

**Unstable (feature `device_profiles`).**

Replace the profiles of a device.

The device applies the profiles in the given order, so later profiles take
precedence. Device credentials cannot change profiles.

**Unstable (feature `device_profiles`).**

Atomically add and remove profiles on explicit devices in one project.

Added profiles apply after the device's other profiles, in the given order.
Adding an assigned profile keeps its position but sets its mode, and removing
an absent one is a no-op. A profile cannot appear in both lists. All devices
and profiles must belong to the project; otherwise no assignments change.
Device credentials cannot change profiles.

**Group `admin`:** Part of the Admin API, which requires instance administrator permissions. Backward-incompatible changes are more frequent than for other actions.

Query the projects of the instance.
Get information about a project.
Create a new project.
Delete a project.

Count the devices of a project.
Query the deployment tokens of a project.

**Group `device`:** Part of the Device API, which Nexigon Agent and other software on devices use. Changes remain backward compatible for at least five years.

Redeem a device pairing key.

Creates a device in the pairing key's project and issues a deployment token bound
to it. The device uses the token to connect to Nexigon Hub. This action does not
require authentication; the pairing key authorizes it.
Query the audit log of the project.
Add a repository to the project.
Remove a repository from the project.
List project definitions and the read-only built-in definitions.

Create or replace a project schema without validating existing property values.

Requires permission to manage project settings. Built-in definitions are read-only.
The schema must be a JSON object or boolean. Editors report unsupported or invalid
schemas and allow explicit overrides; APIs do not enforce schemas on property writes.

Remove a project definition without changing property values.

Requires permission to manage project settings. Built-in definitions are read-only.

**Unstable (feature `otlp_export`).**

Get the OTLP event forwarding configuration for a project.

**Unstable (feature `otlp_export`).**

Set the OTLP event forwarding configuration for a project.

**Group `admin`:** Part of the Admin API, which requires instance administrator permissions. Backward-incompatible changes are more frequent than for other actions.

Query the devices of the instance.
Get information about a device.
Create a new device.
Delete a device.
Set the name of a device.

**Group `device`:** Part of the Device API, which Nexigon Agent and other software on devices use. Changes remain backward compatible for at least five years.

Issue a token that proves a device's identity to an external system.

The token is a JWT signed by Nexigon Hub that carries the device ID and the given
claims. An external backend validates it with `devices_ValidateDeviceToken`.

**Note: Only use this action for integration with external systems.** The token
does not replace the credentials a device uses to connect to Nexigon Hub.

Validate a token issued with `devices_IssueDeviceToken`.

Returns the device ID and claims of a valid token. Tokens of deleted devices, of
devices in deleted projects, and of devices in deactivated organizations are
invalid.

**Note: Only use this action for integration with external systems.**
Add a device certificate.
Delete a device certificate.
Set the status of a device certificate.

Register a connection of a device to a cluster node.

Nexigon Hub invokes this action internally. Clients do not need it.

Unregister a connection of a device to a cluster node.

Nexigon Hub invokes this action internally. Clients do not need it.
Query the connection history of a device.
Issue a HTTP proxy JWT.

Validate an HTTP proxy JWT.

Nexigon Hub invokes this action internally. Clients do not need it.

**Group `device`:** Part of the Device API, which Nexigon Agent and other software on devices use. Changes remain backward compatible for at least five years.

Publish events of a device.

Nexigon Hub stores events as a history of device behavior. Each event has an ID
that is unique per device. An event published again with the same ID is not
stored again, so publishing can safely be retried.
Query device events.

**Group `device`:** Part of the Device API, which Nexigon Agent and other software on devices use. Changes remain backward compatible for at least five years.

Set a property of a device.

A property is a named JSON value of a device. Setting a property replaces the
device's own value and increments the property's version. With an expected version,
the property is only updated if its version still matches (compare-and-swap).
Devices cannot change protected properties.

**Group `device`:** Part of the Device API, which Nexigon Agent and other software on devices use. Changes remain backward compatible for at least five years.

Get a property of a device.

The value combines the values of the device's profiles with the device's own
value.

Remove a property value set on a device.

Values that the device's profiles set for the property remain.
Query the properties of a device.

**Unstable (feature `device_profiles`).**

Query where the property values of a device come from.
Query the audit log of a device.

**Unstable (feature `device_commands`).**

Query the on-demand commands supported by a device.
Set a fleet property manually.
Get a fleet property by name.

Remove a fleet property.

Handles both manual and computed properties. For computed properties, the
associated definition is removed as well.
Query all fleet properties of a project.

**Unstable (feature `fleet_computed_properties`).**

Define a computed fleet property.

**Unstable (feature `fleet_computed_properties`).**

Query computed fleet property definitions for a project.
List the fleet operations of a project, newest first.
Get a fleet operation.
Create a fleet operation as a draft.

Preview the devices that a target selector currently matches.

A preview does not decide the targets of an operation. An operation selects
its targets when it starts and, if it is dynamic, periodically afterwards.

Start a draft fleet operation.

Selects the targets and releases the first stage.

Halt a running fleet operation.

The operation selects no targets, releases no stages, and hands out no work
until it is resumed. Devices can still report the results of work that they
already claimed. The clocks of spreads, soak times, timeouts, and deadlines
do not advance while the operation is halted. Halting a halted operation has
no effect.

Resume a halted fleet operation where it stopped.

Resuming a running operation has no effect.

Release the next stage of a running fleet operation, skipping its guard and
the wait for the previous stage's spread.

Stop a dynamic fleet operation from selecting further targets.

The operation finishes once all of its stages are released and all of its
targets have finished.
Cancel a fleet operation and its unfinished targets.
List the targets of a fleet operation, by stage.

List the devices for which a fleet operation's target selector produced an
error.
Query device operations for a device.
Get device operation details.
Create a device operation.
Start a pending device operation.
Cancel a device operation.

**Group `device`:** Part of the Device API, which Nexigon Agent and other software on devices use. Changes remain backward compatible for at least five years.

Claim device operation work for a device.

Leases pending work items to the device atomically, so no other worker receives
them at the same time. Report the outcome of each item with
`devices_ReportOperationStep`, passing the item's claim ID. Only the device itself
can claim its work.

**Group `device`:** Part of the Device API, which Nexigon Agent and other software on devices use. Changes remain backward compatible for at least five years.

Report the result of a device operation step.

Repeating a report after it was already applied is a successful no-op. A report whose
claim has been superseded is also ignored, so an expired worker cannot overwrite the
current attempt.
Resolve a repository by its name.
Get information about a repository.
Create a new repository.
Delete a repository.
Set the visibility of a repository.
Set the display name of a repository.

Set the slug of a repository.

Note: Setting the slug requires the `public_repositories` subscription feature.
Query the packages of a repository.
Query the assets of a repository.
Configure automatic cleanup. Requires permission to manage repository settings.
List the package attachments retaining a repository asset.
Query repository projects.
Resolve a package by its path.
Get information about a package.
Create a new package.
Delete a package.
Set the name of a package.
Set the kind of a package.
Set metadata on a package.

Replace display text and optionally change the image.
Omitted display name and description are cleared; an omitted image is preserved.

Attach a repository asset to a package under the given filename.

Symmetric to `AddPackageVersionAssetAction` but for the package
itself rather than a specific version. The asset must already exist
in the same repository; the link carries an arbitrary metadata
dictionary.
Remove a package asset by filename.
Replace the metadata on a package asset.
Query a page of the versions of a package, newest first.
Query a page of the tags of a package, most recently assigned first.

**Group `device`:** Part of the Device API, which Nexigon Agent and other software on devices use. Changes remain backward compatible for at least five years.

Resolve a package version by its path.

A path consists of a repository, a package, and a version tag. Devices can resolve
versions in repositories linked to their project.

**Group `device`:** Part of the Device API, which Nexigon Agent and other software on devices use. Changes remain backward compatible for at least five years.

Get information about a package version.
Create a new package version.

Delete a package version.

A version that is the base of another version cannot be deleted.

Permanently seal a version. Requires permission to manage versions.
Sealing cancels scheduled deletion and blocks changes to the name, metadata,
base version, and attachments, as well as deletion of the version, package,
or repository.
Tags remain editable. Sealing cannot be reversed.
Replace the package retention policy. Requires permission to manage versions.

Schedule or cancel automatic deletion. Requires permission to manage versions.
Deletion removes the version and all tags, including locked tags. It does not
check device installations. Unused assets follow the repository cleanup policy.
A version that is the base of another version cannot be scheduled.
Set the name of a package version.

Set or clear the base of a package version. Requires permission to manage versions.

The base must belong to the same package, must not be scheduled for deletion, and
must not lead back to the version through its own bases. Sealed versions reject
changes to their base.
Set metadata on a package version.
Add an asset to a package version.
Remove an asset from a package version.
Set metadata on a package version asset.
Add tags to a version.
Remove tags from a version.

**Group `device`:** Part of the Device API, which Nexigon Agent and other software on devices use. Changes remain backward compatible for at least five years.

Resolve a version asset by its path.

A path consists of a repository, a package, a version tag, and the asset's
filename within the version.
Organization S3 defaults for repositories without their own configuration.
Get organization storage settings. Secret credentials are never returned.
Remove organization storage defaults without deleting stored objects.
Remove a repository override and use organization storage when configured.
Set the S3 configuration for the repository.
Get the S3 configuration for the repository.
Get information about an asset.
Create an asset.

Schedule deletion of an unused asset. Referenced assets are rejected.
The asset remains visible until object-storage deletion completes.

**Group `device`:** Part of the Device API, which Nexigon Agent and other software on devices use. Changes remain backward compatible for at least five years.

Issue a URL for downloading an asset.

The URL is valid for two hours and requires no further authentication.
Issue a URL for uploading an asset.

Verify an uploaded object and make its asset available.

This action is idempotent: finalizing an already available asset succeeds.
Query the audit log of the repository.

**Unstable (feature `vulnerability_management`).**

Trigger indexing of every CycloneDX or SPDX document referenced by the
version's artifact assets via `relations.{sbom,vdr,vex}`.

The hub fetches the referenced documents from the repository's S3
storage and rebuilds the index for this version. The repository
must have S3 configured.

**Unstable (feature `vulnerability_management`).**

Trigger indexing of every CycloneDX or SPDX document referenced by the
package's metadata via `relations.{vex}` (typically just VEX).

Mirrors `IndexVersionDocumentsAction`. Used after attaching a new
package-level VEX asset and pointing the package's metadata at it.

**Unstable (feature `vulnerability_management`).**

Get the vulnerability overview for a package version: artifact list,
SBOM/VDR/VEX descriptors per artifact, package-level VEX, and
(when indexing is enabled) the rolled-up severity summary.

**Unstable (feature `vulnerability_management`).**

Query the components extracted from a package version's SBOMs.
**Unstable (feature `vulnerability_management`).**

nexigon_api.properties.OtaUpdateCapabili.description:
**Unstable (feature `ota_updates`).**

Optional feature of the OTA update contract.

nexigon_api.properties.OtaUpdateConfig.description:
**Unstable (feature `ota_updates`).**

OTA update configuration (`dev.nexigon.ota.config`).

Desired state of a device. Integrations apply the property to defaults
built into the image as a JSON merge patch (RFC 7396): objects merge
recursively, `null` removes a default, and any other value, including an
array, replaces the default.

nexigon_api.properties.OtaUpdateRetryPol.description:
**Unstable (feature `ota_updates`).**

Retry policy for failed update attempts.

An attempt starts when the device begins downloading a version. Failures
before that, such as an unreachable Nexigon Hub, do not count as attempts.
The delay between attempts starts at `initial_delay_secs` and doubles after
each failed attempt, up to `max_delay_secs`.

nexigon_api.properties.OtaUpdateSpread.description:
**Unstable (feature `ota_updates`).**

Spreading of updates across devices.

Each device derives its position `u` from the SHA-256 hash of
`<device-id>/<target-version-id>`: the first 8 bytes, read as a big-endian
unsigned integer `n`, give `u = floor(n / 2^11) / 2^53`, which a
double-precision number represents exactly. A device may start updating to the
target once both of the following hold:

- With `duration_secs`, its turn has begun at
`start + floor(duration_secs * sqrt(u))`. The share of eligible devices
thus grows quadratically from 0 at the start to 1 after `duration_secs`.
- With `percentage`, its position is below `percentage / 100`.

nexigon_api.properties.OtaUpdateState.description:
**Unstable (feature `ota_updates`).**

OTA update state.

The resting states are `idle`, `completed`, `failed`, and `blocked`.
The integration remains in one of these until the next check begins or
the blocking condition clears.

nexigon_api.properties.OtaUpdateStatus.description:
**Unstable (feature `ota_updates`).**

OTA update status (`dev.nexigon.ota.status`).

Actual state of a device, published by its update integration.

The integration writes the status with the version it read last
(compare-and-swap), so that it does not overwrite concurrent changes. Other
writers may only clear `failure_count` and `next_attempt_at`, which requests
a new attempt.

nexigon_api.properties.OtaUpdateWindow.description:
**Unstable (feature `ota_updates`).**

Maintenance window in the device's local time.

The window restricts activation, the step that interrupts the device's
operation, such as the reboot into the new version. Integrations may
download and install an update outside the window if doing so does not
interrupt operation.

nexigon_api.properties.OtaUpdateWindowRa.description:
**Unstable (feature `ota_updates`).**

Recurring time range of a maintenance window.

nexigon_api.properties.OtaUpdater.description:
**Unstable (feature `ota_updates`).**

Update system that installs versions on a device, such as Rugix Ctrl or RAUC.

Slot names, states, and health values are those of the update system.
